newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand plans new measures on offshore borrowing.
newsitem.headline: Thailand plans new measures on offshore borrowing.

text.p: Thai central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Wednesday that new measures were being planned to curb offshore borrowing through the Bangkok International Banking Facility (BIBF).
Such measures, details of which were being worked out, would be aimed at controlling foreign borrowing by the private sector, he told reporters.
"The bank will wait for a suitable time for the introduction of the new measures. We are studying several measures," he said without elaborating.
Thai authorities are keen on curbing foreign borrowing by the private sector because it accounted for the bulk of Thailand's external borrowing.

The Bank of Thailand data showed that Thailand's foreign debt at the end of 1995 totalled $82.6 billion, of which US$66.2 billion was raised by the private sector. The data also showed that $23.7 billion was borrowed through the BIBF.
He said the new measures will mainly focus on the BIBF loans brought in for domestic borrowers, not BIBF loans granted to offshore borrowers.
